items.headline: Lone Star NJROTC Cadets Set Sights on Dual September Physical Challenges
items.summary: The Lone Star Company NJROTC cadets are charging hard into a heavy physical training season as they lock in coordinates for back-to-back community events this month. The group will first stand out as frontline volunteers for the upcoming local 9/11 Heroes Run on September 13, before deploying their top fitness squads to compete in the intensive Tiger Challenge field meet at Stony Point High School on September 19.
items.hook: Austin's Lone Star NJROTC cadets are pushing their physical limits this month between a massive 9/11 honor run and the high-stakes Tiger Challenge drill meet.
items.social: From community service to high-intensity field competitions, these local cadets are setting a massive example this September. Drop a comment to cheer them on!

items.headline: Austin Educator Alasin DeVeny Awarded Mega $50,000 H-E-B Excellence Prize

items.headline: Dell Children’s Hospital Celebrates Historic First Stem Cell Graduate
items.summary: The oncology wing at Dell Children's Medical Center was filled with cheers as their very first pediatric stem cell transplant patient officially rang the victory bell, marking the grand success of a new community-funded program that keeps medical families close to home.
items.hook: A brave local kid just became the very first to ring the cancer-free bell under Dell Children's new homegrown stem cell program.
items.social: No more traveling out of state for specialized care—Central Texas families can now fight and win right here at home. Drop a ❤️ to celebrate this massive milestone!

items.headline: SAFE Alliance Lands Massive $1M Federal Grant to Finish 'The Sasha' Supportive Housing
items.summary: Austin’s SAFE Alliance officially secured a major $1 million federal grant to complete development on 'The Sasha,' a supportive housing facility featuring 60 dedicated residential units designed to give stable, long-term sanctuary to 250 local abuse survivors.
items.hook: A massive one-million-dollar federal injection is going to finish an Austin residential sanctuary for hundreds of abuse survivors.
items.social: Emergency shelters build safety for weeks, but long-term projects like The Sasha change lives forever. Let's celebrate a massive win for Austin non-profits today.
